rotowire.headline: Bueckers finished with 17 points (3-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 10-10 FT), six assists, two blocks, two steals and one rebound in 38 minutes during Friday's 77-73 Game 3 loss to the Valkyries.
rotowire.story: Bueckers struggled mightily from the field in Friday's season-ending loss, though she was effective at the charity stripe and finished as Dallas' second-leading scorer. The star guard also tied for the game-high mark in assists. The 24-year-old had her fair share of struggles in the final two games of this series but was incredible in the regular season, during which she averaged 20.9 points, 5.9 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 1.0 steals across 32.8 minutes per game in 42 outings.
rotowire.description: Bueckers finished with 17 points (3-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 10-10 FT), six assists, two blocks, two steals and one rebound in 38 minutes during Friday's 77-73 Game 3 loss to the Valkyries.

fantasy.projection: Bueckers, one of the most highly-touted prospects in WNBA history, may have somehow exceeded expectations while putting together her impressive rookie resume in 2025. In her Aug. 20 performance versus the Sparks, Bueckers tied the single-game rookie scoring record with 44 points and even became the first player in league history to score at least 40 points while shooting at least 80 percent from the floor. She even led all guards with a 20.3 efficiency rating on the year, averaging 19.2 points, 5.4 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 steals in 33.3 minutes per tilt through 36 regular-season games on her way to running away with the 2025 WNBA Rookie of the Year award. Entering 2026, Bueckers will be trying to take another step forward on a Wings team with several new faces, and she'll work alongside a talented backcourt tandem in Arike Ogunbowale and 2026 No. 1 overall pick Azzi Fudd.
